stories.primary_headline: 'If actors & leaders not safe, then what about citizens?': Firing at Tiger Shroff’s car makes Oppn question Maharashtra govt over law and order

primary_source.headline: 'If actors & leaders not safe, then what about citizens?': Firing at Tiger Shroff’s car makes Oppn question Maharashtra govt over law and order
primary_source.content:
Mumbai: The Opposition on Sunday criticised the Maharashtra government over the firing incident involving Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff’s car in Mumbai, alleging that law and order in the city and state had deteriorated.In a post on X, Congress leader Sachin Sawant said Mumbai appeared to be in the grip of chaos and accused Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, who also heads the Home Department, of failing to maintain law and order.Referring to the murder of former Maharashtra minister Baba Siddique, the firing outside actor Salman Khan’s residence and threats to actors and film producers, Sawant questioned the state government’s efforts to rein in anti-social elements.Fadnavis speaks to Tiger Shroff, asks Mumbai Police commissioner to nab actor's assailants quicklyHe said the situation had reached a point where people who had earlier compared Maharashtra with Bihar were now saying that even Bihar was better.According to police, actor Tiger Shroff escaped unhurt after gunmen opened fire at his car in Mumbai’s Juhu area on Sunday evening. His driver and an autorickshaw driver were injured in the incident, police said.Mumbai Congress president Varsha Gaikwad demanded that Maharashtra have a separate home minister, blaming Fadnavis for the situation.मुंबईत कायदा आणि सुव्यवस्थेचे धिंडवडे!आधी सलमान खानच्या घराबाहेर गोळीबार, त्यानंतर बाबा सिद्दीकी यांची हत्या आणि आता अभिनेता टायगर श्रॉफवर गोळीबार झाल्याची बातमी!मुंबईसारख्या देशाच्या आर्थिक राजधानीत एकापाठोपाठ एक अशा घटना घडत असतील, तर मुंबईकरांच्या सुरक्षेची जबाबदारी नेमकी…&mdash; Prof. Varsha Eknath Gaikwad (@VarshaEGaikwad) October 18, 2026
 

“Does Mumbai have law and order? Does the police still command the same authority and respect as before? Are criminals afraid of the police?” she asked in a video statement.The Lok Sabha member said the Congress had consistently demanded that Maharashtra have a separate home minister.“If actors and political leaders are not safe, what can we say about the safety of ordinary citizens?” she asked.NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar said the incident came days after the recent killing of Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Pradeep Purnekar in Thane.The firing incident involving the actor’s car was alarming, although the actor escaped unhurt, Pawar said.He also said such incidents, including the firing outside the Juhu residence of filmmaker Rohit Shetty, in Mumbai, the country’s financial capital, could undermine investor confidence.Pawar said the home portfolio should be handed over to a “competent minister” if the situation had become difficult to handle.The incident took place near Pushpa Park under Juhu police station limits in the western suburb, and the chain of events leading to the incident is being pieced together, an official said."Shroff is safe and has not sustained any injuries in the firing incident," the official reiterated.

stories.primary_headline: Ranji Trophy | Manvanth Kumar saves the day for Karnataka

primary_source.headline: Ranji Trophy | Manvanth Kumar saves the day for Karnataka
primary_source.content: Bengaluru: An interesting opening day, which began with a strange move of Karnataka fast bowler Vyshak Vijaykumar (1, 5b) walking in at No. 3 in gloomy conditions and Jaydev Unadkat (3/51) and Chetan Sakariya (2/48) reaping some rewards for exploiting pace-friendly conditions, ended with a resilient Manvanth Kumar (86 n.o., 124b) lifting the hosts from a precarious position in their Ranji Trophy game against Saurashtra at the Alur 1 Ground here on Sunday.Arriving at the crease at 187/7 in 50 overs, No. 9 Manvanth, just one first-class game old, showcased his grace and gumption after Aneesh K V’s (59, 96b, 4x8) impressive stay as Karnataka battled hard to reach 281 for eight in 86 overs.Ranji Trophy | Karnataka need batting reset against SaurashtraManvanth hit six fours and five sixes in his unbeaten knock, including one that showed off his elegance, gloriously coming down the track to hit Unadkat down the ground for a maximum.Credit must also go to Abhilash Shetty (6 n.o., 85b), who stuck around with Manvanth, to carve out a late rescue act by stitching an unbeaten 87-run partnership off 206 balls.For Saurashtra, skipper Unadkat, who relentlessly kept it tight, and Parth Bhut (3/73), were the pick of the bowlers.Earlier, the hosts had made as many as five changes, including two debutants, but their batting frailties at the top were again exposed.There was a good amount of movement and bounce on offer for the quicks with Unadkat, in particular, moving the ball at a decent pace in the first session and beating the outside edges at ease.And he did not have to wait long for his first wicket, dismissing Rohan Patil (6) in the fifth over, as the debutant was pinned in front from a ball that cut back in.ExperimentHead coach Vinay Kumar’s experiments continued for a second straight game with Vyshak’s promotion to No.3. The logic behind the move could have been to take the shine off the new ball, but that failed spectacularly. Vyshak was back in the hut within five balls when he was castled after he stepped out and went for a wild swing across the sticks.When Aneesh and Mayank Agarwal (42, 83b) joined hands, Karnataka were two down for not many, with Saurashtra dominating proceedings and making the hosts play and earn every run.While batting wasn’t easy, Aneesh and Mayank portrayed superb application with the rotation of strike and looked more at ease in the middle after surviving some anxious moments.Aneesh, batting for a spot, looked very composed and brought up his third first-class fifty with a single to square leg in 65 balls, and Mayank, with all his experience, respected the good deliveries as Karnataka went into Lunch with 91/2 in 25 overs.After the break, the runs started to dry up, and the hosts lost Agarwal leg before when he shuffled across to flick Unadkat in the 33rd over.It was a bittersweet day for Aneesh, as he followed Mayank three overs later, throwing his wicket while trying to pull a delivery over his head.Karun Nair once again steadied a sinking Karnataka ship with an proactive 46 off 57, laced with nine boundaries, and skipper Shreyas Gopal (3) was sent back with a beautiful Parth delivery that took his edge and into the Sammar Gajjar at slip.Highlights - Shreyas felicitated It was an afternoon of pride and celebration for all-rounder Shreyas Gopal as he was felicitated by the KSCA on Sunday for his 100 first-class appearances.&nbsp; During the Tea break in Karnataka’s Ranji Trophy fixture against Saurashtra in Alur, Shreyas was presented with a special jersey with the No. 100 on the back by KSCA Committee Member Avinash Vaidya.&nbsp; Shreyas’ 100th game came during the Duleep Trophy final between South Zone and East Zone at the M A Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai.SCOREBOARD KARNATAKA (I Innings): Rohan Patil lbw Unadkat 6 (18b 1x4) Mayank Agarwal lbw Unadkat 42 (83b 4x4 1x6) Vyshak Vijaykumar b Sakariya 1 (5b) K V Aneesh c Desai b Sakariya 59 (96b 4x8) Karun Nair c Kotak b Bhut 46 (57b 9x4) Aneeshwar Gautam 4 (2b 1x4) Shreyas Gopal c Gajjar b Bhut 3 (11b) Manvanth Kumar (batting) 86 (124b 6x4 5x6) Abhilash Shetty (batting) 6 (85b). Extras (LB-6 W-1) 7. TOTAL (for 8 wkts 86 overs) 281. Fall of wickets: 1-12 2-13 3-111 4-131 5-140 6-183 7-187 8-194. Bowling: Jaydev Unadkat 19-3-51-3 Chetan Sakariya 18-3-48-2 Ankur Panwar 9-2-30-0 Chirag Jani 8-0-45-0 Parth Bhut 21-3-73-3 Prerak Mankad 9-4-19-0 Sammar Gajjar 2-0-9-0. Other Group B brief scores: At Vijayawada: Hyderabad: 275 all out in 86 overs (Tanmay Agarwal 42 Abhirath Reddy 67 Pragnay Reddy 31 Rahul Radesh 58; Lalith Mohan 3-42 Tripurana Vijay 4-90 Saurabh Kumar 3-75) vs Andhra: 9/0 in 2 overs. At New Chandigarh: Punjab: 269/4 in 90 overs (Vihaan Malhotra 40 Uday Saharan 106 Prabhsimran Singh 62 Sahil Arora 38 n.o.; Dharmendrasinh Jadeja 2-92 Ajay Mandal 2-60) vs Chhattisgarh. At Guwahati: Assam: 228/6 in 86 overs (Nibir Deka 34 Rishav Das 37 Sibsankar Roy 54 Sumit Ghadigaonkar 49; Sandip Sarkar 3-64) vs Tripura.

stories.primary_headline: Tilak Varma relishes new role as finisher

primary_source.headline: Tilak Varma relishes new role as finisher
primary_source.content: Bengaluru: India’s T20I vice-captain Tilak Varma has never shied away from talking his heart out. And for someone who loves pace on the ball and batting at No. 3, dropping down to No. 5 or even No. 6 is not an ideal situation to be in.However, for Tilak, who rarely gets to bat in his preferred position in a changed set-up, versatility has been his biggest strength.&nbsp;Asian Games 2026 | Abhishek Sharma, Tilak Varma do the star turn as India beat Pakistan by 19 runs to defend titleFrom the third T20I against South Africa in Dharamsala in December 2025 to the T20 World Cup (Super Eights vs South Africa) in Ahmedabad in February, Tilak regularly batted at No. 3 for seven straight games.And since his debut, if not on some rare occasion, Tilak has been a standard in India’s T20 top-four. Once Sanju Samson returned to the XI to accompany Abhishek Sharma at the top, and with Ishan Kishan playing one drop, Tilak was pushed down the order as a floating option. He admits that the situation is “unfortunate”, but India’s vice-captain also understands what it means to be a team-player, while enjoying the role of a finisher. “It is not easy to change the numbers (batting) from No. 3 to No. 5 and No. 6. It will be slightly challenging. But I have been working on that, especially how to finish the games. I have said I love finishing the games for India,” Tilak said after the series-deciding fifth T20I was called off due to persistent rain.For me as an individual, if you see, it will be easier batting at 3. But unfortunately, I should bat at 5 or 6 because we have got that combination at the top right now. Kishan (Ishan) is batting at 3, and he is doing brilliantly. I think there is no option but to bat at five or six and do the job."Talking about his role clarity and preparation in his transition to a T20I finisher, Tilak highlighted he’s got all the shots in the book and is confident of changing positions with just a few sessions in the nets. And the numbers are impressive: averaging 65.66 in nine games.“We should do that (working on his skills as a finisher), otherwise, it will be tough. When you go in to bat as a finisher, if the ball comes in your arc, you should try to hit it for a six. Because, if you see in T20s, most of the time in this role, you get to bat a maximum of five or six overs.“If you see, I have been in this role in my childhood as well. Now even if I come back to No. 3, I can adapt within a day or two of practice. I am confident of batting anywhere,” he said.

stories.primary_headline: Mysuru Dasara 2026 | Kambala turns Saathgalli into mini Tulu Naadu

primary_source.headline: Mysuru Dasara 2026 | Kambala turns Saathgalli into mini Tulu Naadu
primary_source.content: Mysuru: Amid all the opposition by activists, two-day Kambala-male buffalo or bulls race which began on Sunday morning, is unravelling mini Tulu Naadu at Saathgalli in Mysuru. A sea of people of all age groups are rushing to the mini fair. They are thrilled to witness 150 pairs of bulls who are splashing the water to the height of upto 7 feet and crossing 145 meter length and 30 meter width Kambala track in lightning speed within seconds. While the races in six segments began around 10 am, Chief Minister D K Shivakumar formally inaugurated it at around 7.30 pm and witnessed the race for about an hour. CM D K Shivakumar said "Kambala is a harvest festival of Coastal region. They started it 800 years praying Kadri Manjunathswamy to protect farmers. In order to showcase all cultures during Naada Habba Mysuru Dasara we are hosting Kambala here to foster the culture. They have put sensors to record the time taken by each buffalo and one had crossed track in nine seconds."Forums urge Kambala buffalo owners to stay away from Mysuru event amid droughtPuttur MLA Ashok Kumar Rai said, "We hosted Kambala in Bengaluru last year. We had planned to host it during Dasara in Mysuru last year itself. We are happy to introduce this coastal culture of Kambala to the people of Mysuru region during Dasara this year." He urged CM for the opportunity to host it in all possible districts across the State.Ashok Kumar Rai said, "The race will conclude on Monday evening. A reward of 16 gram gold, 8 gram gold and 4 gram gold will be given for those winning first, second and third prizes respectively. The owners of each pair of Buffaloes need atleast Rs 3 lakh to bring them here. They spend atleast Rs 12 lakh a year to nourish them. The owners of these buffaloes don't participate in Kambala for prize but to keep up their family name and carry forward the legacy of this culture."He informed, "The bulls which arrived on Saturday evening will be leaving on Tuesday morning. About 5000 assistants have accompanied them. They are accommodated with the buffaloes at the venue. They have brought the food and water for the buffaloes. The state government is spending about Rs 3 crore and they have made all arrangements. They are giving an honorarium of Rs 65,000 for each pair of bigger bulls and Rs 50,000 per pair for smaller bulls."Environmentalists, farmers hold mega protest opposing Kambala amid droughtEven as about half a million liter water is required per day, they have drilled two borewells. He claimed that since it has rained well, the tracks are naturally full and the water consumption has reduced. Ashok Rai also said that the arrangement has been done to accommodate about 15,000 people, but atleast 20,000 people are witnessing the event at a time. By 12 noon 75,000 people had witnessed it at the venue; and 2 million people had watched it online by 2 pm on Sunday.Besides races, people are even enjoying coastal style food including varieties of fishes, Kori rotti, Neerdose at food mela hosted by people of coastal region including those from Mangaluru. Besides grabbing video of races, people are also clicking photos and selfies with buffaloes.85-year-old Lakshmi from Shirsi who had come for Dasara to her daughter's house in Mysuru said, "I had never seen it live though I had seen it on TV and internet, so I was keen to witness it."Mysuru district police led by SP Mallikarjun Balanandi said that they have deployed about 1500 cops for the security to the overnight event. They have installed 50 CCTV cameras and are using four drones too.

stories.primary_headline: Delhi: Class 12 student stabbed to death outside school, five apprehended

primary_source.headline: Delhi: Class 12 student stabbed to death outside school, five apprehended
primary_source.content: New Delhi: A 17-year-old Class 12 student was allegedly stabbed to death outside a government school in southwest Delhi's Mohan Garden area following an altercation between two students over the prescribed school shoes, police said on Sunday.Five accused, including three minors and two adults, have been apprehended in connection with the murder, three of whom are students of the same school, they said.The incident took place on October 14 when a PCR call regarding a stabbing incident near a government school in Mohan Garden was received at 6.10 pm at the local police station. The victim, a resident of Mohan Garden, had sustained stab injuries and was taken to Tarak Hospital, where he succumbed during treatment, the police said.Class 11 student fatally stabbed in south Delhi; two heldAccording to an eyewitness, a Class 12 student of the same school, the dispute began after another student complained to a teacher that he was not wearing the prescribed school-pattern shoes. This led to a heated argument between the two, during which the latter allegedly threatened him.After school hours, when the student left the premises with his friends, including the victim, the other student allegedly instigated the remaining accused, following which the group assaulted them. During the attack, one of the assailants allegedly stabbed the victim, causing fatal injuries, the police said.The knife allegedly used in the crime was recovered near the school gate.The victim's father is an ex-serviceman and is currently employed as a gunman in Gurugram, police said.

stories.primary_headline: The Guardian view on plague in Russia: what is most worrying is the lack of information | Editorial

primary_source.headline: The Guardian view on plague in Russia: what is most worrying is the lack of information | Editorial
primary_source.content: In the three weeks since a health worker’s death in Siberia, officials have stonewalled the WHO – setting a worrying precedent for future pandemicsIs there a plague outbreak in Russia? If the answer were a clear yes, there shouldn’t be much reason to worry. With swift medical intervention, plague is treatable. But in the nearly three weeks since a worker at a Siberian plague research unit died of a mysterious respiratory illness, state officials have been consistently tight-lipped about what happened and whether there were any further cases.It is this uncertainty that has the World Health Organization (WHO) and international community worried: partly because there is a – very small – risk of an outbreak, and partly because it is yet another warning that the international coordination we rely on to prevent pandemics is fraying along with the rest of international politics, and could easily fail to protect us in the future.
